THE ANOMALY TOWARDS THE TOP LEFT CORNER OF THE IMAGE WAS APPROXIMATELY 22.4 NMI IN LENGTH AND 0.3 NMI IN WIDTH. THE ANOMALY TOWARDS THE BOTTOM RIGHT WAS APPROXIMATELY 17.0 NMI IN LENGTH AND 0.9 NMI IN WIDTH. A VESSEL COULD NOT BE IDENTIFIED IN THE IMAGE. THEREFORE, THE CENTER POINT WAS PLACED BETWEEN THE TWO SEGMENTS. THE ANOMALIES HAD A GOOD CONTRAST FROM THEIR SURROUNDINGS AND HAD WELL DEFINED EDGES. THE WINDS AT THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE 5-10 KTS FROM THE SSE. THE ANOMALY IN THE BOTTOM RIGHT ALSO HAD A FEATHERING-LIKE ORIENTATION WHICH AGREED WITH THE WIND DIRECTION. UNCERTAINTIES: THE ANOMALY DID NOT WIDEN APPRECIATIVELY WITH DISTANCE. THERE WAS NO VESSEL IDENTIFIED. DUE TO THESE FACTORS THE CONFIDENCE WAS KEPT AT MEDIUM.

Report Description*****THIS IS AN UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1474201***** UPDATE IS AS FOLLOWS: - DISCHARGE UPDATED FROM POTENTIAL TO ACTUAL - AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF MATERIAL IMPACTED STORM DRAINS ALONG THE ROAD WHICH DAYLIGHTED AT A CREEK ACROSS THE ROAD. THERE WAS NO IMPACT TO THE RETENTION POND. THE PRECISE AMOUNT OF MATERIAL DISCHARGED IN TOTAL AND/OR TO THE STORM DRAIN IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION. THE POTENTIAL AMOUNT DISCHARGED REMAINS 22000 GALLONS. FURTHER INFORMATION ON THE INCIDENT REMAINS LIMITED. - THE FIRE HAS BEEN UPDATED TO EXTINGUISHED. ORIGINAL REPORT BELOW: THE CALLER REPORTED A CATASTROPHIC FAILURE ON AN UNKNOWN PIECE OF EQUIPMENT AT A POWER SUBSTATION, RESULTING IN A FIRE. IT IS UNKNOWN WHAT THE CATASTROPHIC FAILURE WAS, AND THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE IS ALSO UNKNOWN. IT IS UNKNOWN AT THIS TIME IF THERE HAS BEEN ANY RELEASE OF MATERIALS, BUT THERE IS A POTENTIAL FOR A RELEASE OF UP TO 22,000 GALLONS OF NON-PCB TRANSFORMER OIL. THE SOURCE OF WHERE THE MATERIALS WOULD RELEASE FROM IS UNKNOWN. IT IS UNKNOWN IF THE FIRE HAS BEEN EXTINGUISHED. IF MATERIALS WERE TO RELEASE, THEY WOULD RELEASE ONTO A GRAVEL BED AND INTO A RETENTION POND, WITH POTENTIAL TO REACH BEAVER RUIN CREEK ABOUT 3200 FEET AWAY.
